observations.cause: sentencepiece 0.2.2 fails internlm2's SentencePiece->fast conversion outright: 'Converting from SentencePiece and Tiktoken failed'. RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.ROOT_CAUSE_RESEARCHED_20260812: vLLM HAS NO NATIVE RECURRENTGEMMA IMPLEMENTATION AT ANY VERSION. `RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM` is absent from vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py at v0.27.1 and at every version checked back to v0.4.1, and absent from the explicit _TRANSFORMERS_BACKEND_MODELS allow-list. When an architecture is not in the registry and model_impl=='auto' (the DEFAULT), resolve_model_cls falls through to _try_resolve_transformers(), which pulls the class from the installed `transformers` package and runs it via TransformersForCausalLM. vLLM's own docs state there is NO WARNING that this is fallback behaviour. So we were never running vLLM's code -- we were running HuggingFace's reference PyTorch, whose RG-LRU scan is a literal per-timestep Python loop (`for t in range(...): recurrent_states = gate[:,t]*recurrent_states + x[:,t]`). Google's own recurrentgemma repo says the FLAX path uses a low-level Pallas fused kernel and the PyTorch one is 'un-optimized... for reference'.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.why_the_symptoms_fit: Sequential small-kernel launches are launch-bound, not compute-bound: the card idles between hundreds of tiny elementwise kernels, which is exactly a steady 20-28% utilisation. And SCORING is disproportionately worse than generation because prompt_logprobs teacher-forcing is pure PREFILL over the full stored sequence -- entirely the O(seq_len) loop, with no O(1)-per-token decode phase to amortise it.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.cheap_wins: NONE FOUND. Batch width does not reduce the number of sequential timesteps. VLLM_USE_V1 targets the native hybrid/Mamba cache path, which this model never enters because it is not registered at all.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.alternatives: JAX/Flax official repo is the ONLY path with a source-confirmed FUSED kernel (Pallas). MLX has recurrentgemma.py but with the SAME Python-loop scan, and its batch_generate does not expose per-token logprobs (open issue ml-explore/mlx-lm#1358). llama.cpp does NOT support the architecture at all (issue #6564 closed unimplemented; llama-arch.cpp has no Griffin entry). HF transformers directly is the same code vLLM already falls back to.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.unknown: Whether the Pallas RG-LRU kernel runs on non-TPU. And NO public RecurrentGemma GPU tokens/sec figure exists anywhere, so our ~255 tok/s is uncompared.

measured_padding._note: MEASURED on the box 12 Aug, not inferred. The gap between embedding rows and tokenizer pieces IS the defect: every id in it passes a model-vocab guard and crashes IdToPiece.

sentencepiece_out_of_range.fix_is_load_bearing: CONFIRMED by measurement rather than by the run completing. Three of the four arms have a real padding gap, so the corrected min() bound differs from the old one and the ids it newly excludes are exactly the ones that raise IdToPiece. Teuken's INSTRUCT arm has no gap -- the pair is protected by its BASE arm's bound, which is why a per-pair check must look at both arms and not one.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.how_to_check_any_pair: len(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(m)) < AutoConfig.from_pretrained(m).vocab_size -> the pair is exposed. Cheap, needs no weights, and answers it before a box is rented.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.fix_DEMONSTRATED: OBSERVED FIRING 12 Aug on Teuken: '723/4096 dropped: id >= scorer vocab 250680'. 250,680 is the TOKENIZER's piece count; the old guard would have used the base arm's 250,880 embedding rows, let those 723 sequences through, and raised IdToPiece. This is the fix doing the work, not the pair getting lucky.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.ct_llm_did_NOT_exercise_it: CT-LLM completed with ZERO drop lines. Its recovery is therefore NOT evidence for the fix -- different box, different card, different sampled ids. Two pairs recovered, only ONE of them tests the guard. Do not cite CT-LLM as confirmation.

The fix converts a CRASH into MISSINGNESS, which is the right trade but is not free: expect Teuken to carry a high unscorable rate, in the Aquila2 class rather than the 0.03% corpus norm. Per-pair denominators, not the corpus mean.
